expectation: Replay preserves namespaced function and matching result.
Pre-created quota rejection uses alternate without historical metadata as a confounder.
Plaintext agent history remains usable without historical developer metadata.
Visible text is delivered once; quota error does not trigger cross-account replay.
Ordinary continuation succeeds on the healthy original owner.
Failed replacement cannot strand identical history when a third account becomes eligible.
Real prewarm suffix can recover capacity with one coherent downstream response.
Two successive handoffs retain later plaintext agent input and original client turn token.
Plaintext agent delivery after settled tool output does not prevent quota handoff.
Opaque agent suffix does not qualify through the plaintext portability path.
Agent delivery cannot replace a missing tool result.
An anchor-only delta cannot be relocated without history reconstruction.
Historical developer instructions survive a full-history quota handoff and follow-up.
HTTP quota rejection with plaintext agent history can hand off.
ID-less pre-created response.failed quota envelope is recoverable; exact raw upstream provenance remains unverified.
Agent input in the stored prefix survives two handoffs.
A replacement reconnect after completion stays on its owner and later handoff works.
A mismatched history does not reuse proof of the old prefix.
A missing result cannot be hidden by later user input.
Opaque agent content in the stored prefix does not qualify as plaintext.
Created response does not enter the pre-created quota handoff path.
